app.name: Statbis Lab
toolbar.privacy: Your data stays in this browser
toolbar.privacyHelp: Nothing you paste is uploaded or saved. Closing or reloading the page clears it.
examples.ex01_describe_delivery: Delivery times — descriptive statistics and charts
examples.ex02_ci_basket: Basket value and vouchers — confidence intervals
examples.ex03_onesample_waiting: Waiting times vs a target — one-sample tests
examples.ex04_twosample_channel: Basket value by channel — two-sample t-test
examples.ex05_paired_promo: Units sold before and after a promo — paired t-test

grid.levelButton: {level} — click to change the name, level or unit of {name}
grid.emptyHelp: Type the variable names in the first row and the data below them. Or copy a table from Excel or Google Sheets (names in the first row), click the first cell and press Ctrl+V.
grid.emptyExamples: No data at hand? Open Example data.
grid.fingerprintHelp: A code computed from the pasted values. The same data always gives the same code, so an assistant who pastes your sheet can check that your report came from it. Renaming variables does not change it.
warn.headerNumeric: The first row looks like numbers, but it was used as the variable names. If your table has no row of names, add one in Excel and paste again.
warn.coded: {name}: is this a coded category (1 = Male, 2 = Female)? Change it to nominal in the variable dialog.
warn.id: Looks like an ID column; it cannot be used as a grouping variable.
warn.codedShort: Is this a coded category? Click the type label in the grid to change it to nominal.
warn.nonNumeric: {name}: {count} cells are not numbers and count as missing.
paste.empty: The clipboard holds no table. Copy cells from Excel or Google Sheets first.
paste.noRows: Only one row was pasted. The first row must hold the variable names and the rows below it the data.
confirm.replaceBody: The data in the grid will be replaced by the new table.
confirm.newBody: The data in the grid will be removed.
confirm.reportCleared: Everything in the report will also be cleared. Download or print it first if you need it.
variable.title: Variable
variable.name: Name
variable.ratioHelp: Needed for the coefficient of variation (CV).
variable.nameTaken: Another variable already has this name.
settings.title: Settings
settings.invalidHelp: Cells holding one of these codes count as missing, as do empty cells. One code per line. This list resets when the page is reloaded.
settings.decimalHelp: Auto reads each column the way it is written, and shows results with a comma in Bahasa Indonesia and a point in English. Comma or Point applies to both reading and showing.
tabs.label: Analyses
picker.noData: Paste data above to choose variables.
section.comingSoon: The results for this tab are still being built.
report.title: Report
report.clearConfirm: Remove every item from the report?
report.empty: Nothing here yet. Use Add to report under any table or chart.
report.notSaved: Not saved — download or print before closing this page.
dev.demoInterpretation: This table lists each ticked variable with the number of usable values (n used) and the number of missing cells (n excluded). It exists only to test Copy, Interpretation and Add to report.
dev.tickSomething: Tick a variable to see the demo table.
grid.label: Data table
grid.help: Click a cell and type, or paste a block with Ctrl+V. Right-click to insert or delete rows and columns; Ctrl+Z undoes.
grid.notSaved: Nothing is saved: use Copy data to keep your edits in Excel or Google Sheets.
notice.dataCopied: The whole table is on the clipboard. Paste it into Excel or Google Sheets to keep it.
notice.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying. Select the cells and press Ctrl+C instead.
confirm.editsLost: Your edits are not saved anywhere. Use Copy data first if you want to keep them.
variable.valuesHint: To change values, edit the cells in the grid. Changing the name, level or unit never changes the data.
report.staleNote: Made from an earlier version of the data (fingerprint {fingerprint}); the data was edited afterwards.
